chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to him, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to me, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Husayn al-Farsi narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon them).
He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Nothing has been combined with anything better than forbearance with knowledge.'

key_terms.حِلْم: Forbearance, patience, or gentleness in the face of provocation
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family
key_terms.عِلْم: Knowledge, specifically religious or divine knowledge

ai.seo_question: What is the best combination of character traits according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on the integration of intellectual depth (*'ilm*) with moral character (*hilm*), a cornerstone of the ideal believer's profile. It suggests that knowledge without patience leads to arrogance, while patience without knowledge lacks direction, making their union the highest spiritual achievement. This pairing reflects the Prophetic ideal of balancing cognitive insight with emotional regulation, essential for effective leadership and personal piety.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-10 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleasedwith him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Abil-Hussein al-Farsi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali (MGB)
that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “Nothing has been combined with anything better than forbearance with knowledge.”
